introduction: Today, on the last Sunday of the liturgical year, we celebrate Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe. Daniel sees one like a son of man receiving an everlasting kingdom. The Book of Revelation proclaims Jesus the ruler of the kings of the earth, who loves us and freed us from our sins. In the Gospel, Jesus stands before Pilate and says, My Kingdom is not of this world. Let us give our lives to Christ our King.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ is the faithful witness, who loves us and has freed us from our sins. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may bear witness to the truth and serve the Kingdom of Christ in the world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who govern nations: that they may seek justice, truth and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who suffer under unjust power, and for prisoners of conscience: that Christ the King may give them strength and freedom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are searching for the truth: that they may listen to the voice of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that Christ may reign in our hearts, our homes and our work. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty God, you have given all dominion to your Son, the King of the universe. May all creation serve him, and may his Kingdom of truth and love come in our hearts. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: My Kingdom is not of this world
reflection.body:
The Church's year ends with a feast of Christ the King, established by Pope Pius XI in 1925 at a time when new powers claimed total control over people's lives. The feast says: there is only one King to whom we owe our whole lives, and his rule is different from every other.

Daniel sees a vision of "one like a son of man" coming with the clouds, who receives from God "Dominion... with glory and a kingdom, that all the peoples, nations, and languages should serve him." His kingdom will never be destroyed.

The Book of Revelation tells us who this king is and how he reigns: "Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth." He rules by love: "To him who loves us, and washed us from our sins by his blood." And he shares his reign with us: "he made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God and Father."

In the Gospel, Jesus stands bound before Pilate, the representative of the most powerful empire on earth. Pilate asks, "Are you the King of the Jews?" Jesus answers, "My Kingdom is not of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight." His kingdom does not rest on armies or force. Then he says why he came: "that I should testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice."

The King of the universe stands as a prisoner, and soon he will be crowned with thorns. His throne is the cross. That is how he wins our hearts.

As the year ends, ask yourself: who or what really rules my life? Give Christ a place on the throne of your heart again. And listen for his voice, which speaks the truth.
